section_summary.extract_value: This section explores the relationship between self-esteem and self-deception, specifically self-deceptive enhancement (SDE). It highlights that SDE, measured by the BIDR, is linked to maladaptive behaviors and negative social outcomes, mirroring findings for high self-esteem. A positive correlation (r=.45) is noted between SDE and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), suggesting that self-esteem might be maintained through self-deceptive mechanisms. The current studies aim to address this conflation by comparing a more differentiated model of self-evaluation to self-deceptive enhancement.
